# Normalising constant estimation using importance sampling

Suppose we have two unnormalised probability densities, $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ corresponding to distributions $F$ and $G$. We can compute the ratio of their normalising constants if we have samples from one of them. (Can we get a better estimator if we have samples from both??)

$$Z_2 = \int g(x) dx$$

and $$\tilde g(x) = \frac{g(x)}{Z_2}$$

Now,
\begin{align*}
Z_1 &= \int f(x) dx\\
&= \int \frac{f(x)}{g(x)} g(x) dx \\
&= Z_2 \cdot \int \frac{f(x)}{g(x)} \tilde g(x) dx \\
\frac{Z_1}{Z_2} &= \mathbb E_{G} \Bigg[\frac{f(X)}{g(X)}\Bigg] = q_{1,2}
\end{align*}

This is an expectation with respect to the distribution G. If we have samples $x_1, x_2 \dots x_N \sim G$, we can estimate $q_{1,2}$ using

$$\hat q_{1,2} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N} w(x_i) $$

where $w(x_i) = \frac{f(x_i)}{g(x_i)}$ is identical to the self-normalised importance sampling weights.

Similarly,
$$\frac{Z_2}{Z_1} = \mathbb E_{F} \Bigg[\frac{g(Y)}{f(Y)}\Bigg] = q_{2,1}$$ 

This is an expectation with respect to the distribution F. If we have samples $y_1, y_2, \dots y_M \sim F$, we can estimate $q_{2,1}$ using:

$$\hat q_{2,1} = \frac{1}{M} \sum_{i=1}^{M} v(y_i)$$ where $v(y_i) = \frac{g(y_i)}{f(y_i)}$


Suppose we know one of the normalising constants by analytical integration or some other way, say $Z_2$. Then we can easily come up with an estimate of the other using our estimate of the ratio. $$\hat Z_1 = \hat q_{1,2}\cdot Z_2$$

It would be interesting to see if the estimator $\hat q = \sqrt{\frac{\hat q_{1,2}}{\hat q_{2,1}}}$ is a better estimator of the ratio $q_{1,2}$ than just $\hat q_{1,2}$.

Well it appears- not quite.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
### F ~ N(0, 1), G ~ N(0, 4)

set.seed(42)
sigma_1 <- 1
sigma_2 <- 2

N <- 1000
n <- 10000

Q <- rep(0, n)
Q_fw <- rep(0, n)
Q_bw <- rep(0, n)

for(i in 1:n){
  X <- rnorm(N, 0, sd = sigma_2) # ~G
  Y <- rnorm(N, 0, sd = sigma_1) # ~F
  
  q_12 <- mean(exp(-0.5*X^2/sigma_1^2)/exp(-0.5 * X^2/sigma_2^2))
  q_21 <- mean(exp(-0.5*Y^2/sigma_2^2)/exp(-0.5 * Y^2/sigma_1^2))
  q <- sqrt(q_12/q_21)

  Q[i] <- q
  Q_fw[i] <- q_12
  Q_bw[i] <- 1/q_21
}

# compute densities
dQ    <- density(Q)
dQ_fw <- density(Q_fw)
dQ_bw <- density(Q_bw)

plot(dQ_fw, col = "orange", lwd = 2,
     main = "Distribution of Q, Q_fw, and Q_bw",
     xlab = "Value", ylab = "Density", xlim = c(0.4, 0.6), ylim = c(0, 35))

abline(v = 0.5)
lines(dQ, col = "brown", lwd = 2)
lines(dQ_bw, col = "red", lwd = 2)

legend("topright", legend = c("Q_fw", "Q", "Q_bw", "truth"),
       col = c("orange", "brown", "red", "darkgreen"), lwd = 2, bty = "n")
```
